content: 1. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are prescribed to help patients achieve personalized glycemic control while also offering cardiovascular protective effects. 2. Nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) are indicated for use in patients with persistent albuminuria, defined as an albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR) of ≥30 mg/g, provided that serum potassium levels remain within the normal range. 3. 4. Antiplatelet agents are recommended for individuals with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) to reduce the risk of recurrent cardiovascular events. 5. Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 inhibitors (PCSK9i) or ezetimibe are employed for lipid management in patients who fail to achieve their low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) targets despite maximally tolerated statin therapy.
